environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed on EC2 but origin access is exclusively through a CloudFront distribution configured with Origin Access Control (OAC) using SigV4 signing. The origin (ALB) has a custom header validation rule (x-origin-verify) that rejects requests not originating from the CloudFront distribution. CloudFront is configured with a Trusted Key Group for signed URL generation — all requests to /api/v2/documents/* require a valid CloudFront signed URL with a policy restricting the upload payload size to 1024 bytes via a custom CloudFront Function that inspects Content-Length. The CloudFront Function (viewer-request trigger) additionally validates that the request body content-length does not exceed the signed policy's size constraint, effectively capping uploaded archives at 1KB. The EC2 security group only allows inbound traffic from CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). Container runs as non-root uid 1001 with a read-only root filesystem; the /var/app/uploads path is a tmpfs mount with noexec and a 512KB size limit.

config.cloudfront_function: viewer-request trigger enforcing Content-Length <= 1024 from signed policy custom field
config.filesystem: read-only rootfs, tmpfs at /var/app/uploads with noexec,size=512k
